questions.q: The keyboard shortcut to increase the indent of a paragraph in MS Word is:
questions.solution: Ctrl+M increases indent, Ctrl+Shift+M decreases it. (Tab indents only at the start of a paragraph/list item; Ctrl+I is italic.)
questions.shortcut: M = More indent; add Shift = less.

questions.q: Which key **edits the active cell** in Excel?
questions.solution: **F2** puts the cell in edit mode — the keyboard version of a double-click.

questions.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+J applies which alignment to the selected paragraph?
questions.solution: Ctrl+J justifies text so both margins are straight. Left is Ctrl+L, centre is Ctrl+E and right is Ctrl+R.

questions.q: **PDF** (the extension .pdf) stands for —
questions.solution: **Portable Document Format** — a fixed-layout document that looks identical on every device, opened in readers like Adobe Reader or a browser.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The workers ___ on this bridge for two years now.
questions.solution: 'For two years' measures a duration that continues to the present → present perfect continuous **have been working**.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Either Ram or his brothers ___ to blame for the loss.
questions.solution: Nearer subject = brothers (plural) → **are**.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The prize money was divided ___ the two winners.
questions.solution: Two parties → **between**; three or more treated as a mass → among.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** Food is wasted at almost every Indian wedding. **P:** Meanwhile, thousands in the same city go to bed hungry. **Q:** Much of the leftover food ends up in the garbage. **R:** Hosts often cook for far more guests than actually attend. **S:** Clearly, the extra food must reach those who need it. **6.** Several groups now collect wedding leftovers for night shelters.
questions.solution: **S** begins with 'Clearly' and concludes from everything before it, so it is last. **Q**'s 'the leftover food' needs the extra cooking in **R**. **P**'s 'Meanwhile' contrasts hunger with the waste already described. **RQPS**.
questions.shortcut: 'Clearly' marks the closing part; cause -> waste -> contrast before it.

questions.q: Ustad **Amjad Ali Khan** is a maestro of the —
questions.solution: **Amjad Ali Khan** — sarod; the senia-maihar lineage of his family is famous for it.

questions.q: When **blue copper sulphate crystals** are heated strongly, they —
options: Turn white as water of crystallisation is lost
questions.solution: Heating drives off the 5H₂O; the anhydrous CuSO₄ left behind is **white** — and turns blue again if moistened.

questions.q: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra was formed by:
questions.solution: **Lonar** (Buldhana district) sits in a crater made by a **meteorite impact** on the basalt of the Deccan Trap.

questions.q: The average lifespan of a human **red blood cell** is —
questions.solution: **120 days** — the spleen then recycles them, hence its nickname 'graveyard of RBCs'.

questions.q: The standard deviation of a set of observations is 7. If each observation is multiplied by 3 and then 5 is added, the new standard deviation is:
questions.solution: SD$(3x + 5) = 3 \times 7 = 21$ — the shift never affects spread.

questions.q: The value of $\sin^2 14^\circ + \sin^2 31^\circ + \sin^2 59^\circ + \sin^2 76^\circ$ is:
questions.solution:
$\sin 76^\circ = \cos 14^\circ$ and $\sin 59^\circ = \cos 31^\circ$ (each pair sums to $90^\circ$).

So the sum $= (\sin^2 14^\circ + \cos^2 14^\circ) + (\sin^2 31^\circ + \cos^2 31^\circ) = 1 + 1 = 2$.
questions.shortcut: Re-pair into two $\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1$ groups. Trap: $1$ — there are TWO independent pairs here.

questions.q: A can complete a work in 20 days and B in 15 days. A works alone for 5 days, after which B joins him. In how many days in total is the work completed?
questions.solution:
A alone did $\frac{5}{20} = \frac14$. Remaining $\frac34$ at $\frac{7}{60}$/day → $\frac{45}{7} = 6\frac37$ days.
Total $= 5 + 6\frac37 = 11\frac37$ days.

questions.q: Five years ago, the average age of a husband and wife was 25 years. Today, the average age of the husband, the wife and their child is 22 years. The age of the child is:
questions.solution: Couple's total now $= 2 \times 25 + 10 = 60$. Family total $= 3 \times 22 = 66$. Child $= 6$ years.
questions.shortcut: 16 forgets that the couple aged 5 years each.

questions.q:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

**2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ?**
questions.solution: Each term = sum of the previous two: 8 + 13 = 21, so next = 13 + 21 = **34**.

questions.q: A square sheet is folded in half from left to right, and one hole is punched exactly on the folded edge (the crease), halfway up. How many holes does the opened sheet have?
questions.solution: A punch on a crease makes no separate copy: the mirror image of the hole across the fold line falls on the same spot, so the two plies open as just **1** hole, on the crease.
questions.shortcut: Holes = sum of the layers under each punch.

questions.q:
In each triangle the corners are (left, right, top) and a number sits in the centre:

**(2, 3, 4) → 20**

**(1, 5, 3) → 18**

**(4, 2, 5) → ?**
questions.solution: Product of corners fails (24 ≠ 20), sum fails (9). Rule: centre = (left + right) × top: (2 + 3) × 4 = 20 ✓, (1 + 5) × 3 = 18 ✓. So (4 + 2) × 5 = **30**. (40 is the product of all three corners.)
questions.shortcut: Centre just below the corner product → try (x + y) × z.

questions.q:
A survey of **100 people** on how they get news — Newspaper (N), TV (T) and Radio (R) — gave these region counts:

- Only N: 20 · Only T: 25 · Only R: 5
- N and T only: 15 · T and R only: 6 · N and R only: 4
- All three: 10 · None of the three: 15

How many people use **exactly one** source?
questions.solution: Exactly one = only N + only T + only R = 20 + 25 + 5 = **50**. 65 wrongly adds the 15 who use none; 35 is the at-least-two count.
